title: IETF Administration LLC 2027 Draft Budget
description: The IETF Administration LLC has prepared its draft budget for 2027 and now seeks community feedback.

title: France Blames Iran’s Revolutionary Guards for Cyberattack on 700 Supermarkets
description: France has blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards for cyberattacks on refrigeration systems at approximately 700 supermarkets, prompting a criminal investigation, planned European sanctions and warnings about internet-connected industrial equipment.

title: The Cyber Pandemic Is Here: Negligence, Not AI, Is the Real Threat
description: Cyberattacks on supermarkets, utilities and cryptocurrency platforms reveal how unclear responsibilities and institutional failures can expose critical systems, raising questions about accountability across cybersecurity, supply chains and Internet governance.

title: Launching the Vite Ecosystem Fund
description: Cloudflare is distributing the first $301,300 of the Vite Ecosystem Fund to open source projects and maintainers. The recipients were chosen by a panel of Vite stack core team members, including maintainers not employed by Cloudflare.

title: Your Router Trusts Its Validator. But Who's Watching the Validator?
description: ROV turned your validator into a forwarding policy source. The registries have strengthened their side of the RPKI, but the chain from repository to router runs on your infrastructure. When that chain breaks, it often breaks silently.

title: The DOs and don’ts of post-quantum DNSSEC
description: Post-quantum signatures could dramatically enlarge DNSSEC responses, shifting many queries from UDP to TCP. Should resolvers limit unnecessary DNSSEC data, or is greater TCP use inevitable?

title: ITU Meeting in Doha to Consider Proposals Affecting Global Internet Governance
description: Governments meeting in Doha will consider proposals to revise how international telecommunications regulations are reviewed, raising questions about the ITU's responsibilities and their relationship with existing Internet governance organizations.

title: More Than 80% of AfriNIC Addresses Detected Outside Africa Linked to a Single Company
description: New measurements link Cloud Innovation to 81% of AfriNIC IPv4 addresses detected outside Africa, raising questions about regional allocation policies, contractual obligations and the evidence needed to establish compliance.

title: Beyond Blind Trust: Rethinking AI Governance for Operational Resilience
description: As autonomous AI agents gain access to critical systems, a proposed governance framework combines risk-based verification, API restrictions, model provenance and infrastructure safeguards to balance security costs with operational resilience.

title: Can an Open-Source Project Have Unregistered Trademark Rights? Lessons from LIBBITCOIN
description: A WIPO decision involving the LIBBITCOIN open-source project illustrates how community recognition can establish unregistered trademark rights and how documented stewardship can support a successor maintainer's standing in domain name disputes.

title: AI Agents and the End of Endpoint Privacy
description: AI agents with access to decrypted messages pose new challenges for end-to-end encryption, raising questions about endpoint privacy, operating-system permissions and whether users can protect conversations when their correspondents enable AI assistants.

title: The post-quantum future of web privacy
description: Cryptographic protocols like Privacy Pass help keep web sites safe from abuse while keeping their users private. This post looks at the quantum threat to these protocols, and some new post-quantum cryptography that may help close the gap.

title: The Internet's New Factories
description: AI factories create several traffic systems at once, and power is shaping where they can be built. This article asks what operators can see, what stays private, and who decides how these systems are connected.

title: PCAP-LM: Helping AI assistants read network traffic
description: Guest Post: Packet captures are the ground truth of network operations, but analysing them is slow, requires specialist expertise, and does not scale. PCAP-LM rewrites captures into a form that AI assistants can read, helping address that mismatch.

title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
description: AI agents act for millions, but servers see intermediaries that strip user visibility. This post defines the problem space and introduces a collaborative approach to safely identifying, allowing, and managing this automated traffic.

title: ICANN Outlines Internet Governance Agenda for IGF 2026
description: ICANN outlines its IGF 2026 agenda in Nairobi, focusing on multilingual Internet access, multistakeholder governance and Africa's technical community, with discussions on Universal Acceptance, new gTLDs and participation following the WSIS+20 review.

title: Finnish Court Jails Two Ship Crew Members for Baltic Sea Cable Damage
description: A Finnish court sentences two cargo ship crew members to prison for damaging Baltic Sea telecommunications cables, addressing criminal responsibility and jurisdiction over critical infrastructure beyond territorial waters.

title: AFRINIC, Member Rights and Executive Interference
description: AFRINIC's effort to remove Cloud Innovation from its company register has intensified a dispute over court orders, membership rights, executive authority, and the accountability of Internet number registry administrators.

title: Do Registrars Use DNSSEC on Their Own Domains?
description: Registrars must support DNSSEC for customers, but how many use it themselves? A study of 698 registrar domains finds fewer than one in ten has a DS record, with European registrars ahead of the rest. Tobias Sattler explores the gap and its possible explanations.

title: The Internet didn’t break; we just forgot what it was leaning on
description: Guest Post: When international links fail, hidden dependencies can take local services with them. Here’s how operators can design for local resilience.

title: See the agents, set the terms: New visibility and control for personal agents
description: Personal AI agents have changed how users interact with the web, blurring the lines between automated and human traffic. Learn how Cloudflare gives site owners visibility and control to manage personal agent access.

title: The RIPE Chair Team Reports - Highlights from RIPE 93
description: From digital independence and practical AI to inclusion and research, RIPE 93 gave the community plenty to discuss and act on. The RIPE Chair Team shares personal highlights from Sofia and ways to get involved in the work ahead.

title: Solar PV for Internet resilience (Part 1): Designing your system
description: Guest Post: Solar photovoltaics and battery storage can provide reliable power for network infrastructure, even in remote locations. Here’s what’s good to know before selecting equipment.

title: Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities
description: Zero Wire on Cloudflare Radar pairs plain-language briefings with global attack telemetry and remediation steps. Triage critical CVEs faster and decide how to protect your infrastructure.

title: Restating the case for DNSSEC
description: Does TLS make DNSSEC unnecessary? An examination of common DNSSEC assumptions challenges that argument and considers DNSSEC's role in establishing trust, the risks of partial deployment, and the evidence from real-world outages.

title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85%
description: Zone setting changes used to rebuild entire DNS zones, even ones with tens of millions of records. Here is how we built a planner that picks the smallest safe build, cutting full builds by 40%, peak memory by 85%, and halving build delay.

title: APRICOT 2027 registration is now open, with discounts for APNIC Members
description: Registration for the APRICOT 2027 Summit, being held from 24 February to 4 March 2027 in Hong Kong SAR, China, is now open. All registrations and payments completed on or before 15 November 2026 receive the early bird rate.

title: 4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys
description: Four, just four: that’s the key to break into any unpatched connection on the Internet that is using eMudhra certificates. Here’s how we quickly patched Cloudflare, what evidence we can see of attempted exploitation, and how much of the rest of the Internet remains exposed.

title: Cloudflare services for private origins is now generally available
description: Public traffic to private origins, with WAF, bot management, caching, and Workers, is now available to every customer with Cloudflare One connectivity.

title: Suggested IETF 127 Sessions for Getting Familiar with New Topics
description: These IETF 127 meeting sessions are likely to include discussions and proposals that are accessible to a broad range of Internet technologists whether they are new to the IETF or long-time participants.

title: Same place, different view: How VPNs shape what we learn about the Internet
description: Guest Post: A study found that changing VPN providers can change where web traffic appears to be served, affecting conclusions about domestic infrastructure, cross-border traffic, and data localization.

title: Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants
description: Cloudflare mitigated over 8,200 DDoS attacks per hour in Q3 2026 as attackers shifted to shorter, high-frequency strikes. Explore the latest threat data, including the collapse of CLDAP vectors and the impact of recent botnet takedowns.

title: APNIC updates conference host and location selection process
description: APNIC has updated its conference host and location selection process for stand-alone conferences to give prospective hosts clearer guidance and make assessment and decision-making more transparent.

title: [Podcast] Quad9 — Measurement in the privacy-preserving public DNS service
description: Darren Kara discusses how the Quad9 Public DNS server balances privacy, measurement, and global threat intelligence to help protect users from malicious destinations.

title: Global Internet infrastructure at NANOG 98
description: Hyperscaler investment in submarine cables and the rise of LEO satellite systems are reshaping who builds, owns, and operates the networks that underpin global connectivity.

title: Introducing the Cloudflare PHP Capture the Flag challenge
description: We are launching a PHP Capture the Flag challenge integrated with our Bug Bounty program to test our WAF protections. Security researchers are invited to bypass our defenses and capture the flag to help make the Internet safer.

title: SIDN Publishes RSSAC002 Traffic Metrics for .nl
description: SIDN Labs has released open DNS traffic data for .nl in the same format used by root server operators. In this guest post, they explain what they’re sharing and how it opens up new comparisons across the DNS.

title: RIPE 93 Daily Meeting Blog
description: RIPE 93 has kicked off in Sofia - city of wisdom, Roman ruins, and yellow brick roads. As always, you can view the slides, you can watch the recordings, but if you want to get to the bottom of what's really going on, read this daily meeting blog!

description: More local peering, stronger routing security and a shared ambition to improve connectivity: CAPIF 5 brought Central Asia’s Internet community to Dushanbe to compare progress, discuss persistent challenges and learn from the people building the region’s networks.

description: ARIN 58 is almost here — and whether you’re joining us in Miami or signing on from your living room, a little preparation goes a long way. Here’s your TL;DR guide to everything you need to know before ARIN 58 kicks off next week on Thursday, 22 October.

description: The ARIN Advisory Council’s Policy Engagement Working Group shares its progress on implementing the results of the community engagement survey into tangible opportunities to participate in the Policy Development Process.

description: October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month. ARIN Chief Information Security Officer Christian Johnson shares a quick reminder about the value of taking a few minutes to do some basic account housekeeping every now and then.

description: Prepare for the upcoming meeting with this look at the Draft Policies on the agenda at ARIN 58, taking place 22-23 October in Miami, Florida, and online.

description: Anyone can help shape the policies that govern Internet number resources in the ARIN region. Here’s how to submit a policy proposal, read a Draft Policy page, and make your voice heard at our next Public Policy and Members Meeting.

title: Get Ready for ARIN Elections
description: The 2026 ARIN Elections are approaching, making this a good time to review the process and the participation opportunities available to you and your organization. Here’s a step-by-step guide to help you prepare to cast your vote this fall.

description: New features implemented on RFC-Editor.org aim to make the site more useful and engaging for RFC consumers.

description: The days may be shortening as we enter fall at ARIN HQ in Virginia, but we’re not slowing down the steady pace of changes, upgrades, and outreach that cropped up throughout July, August, and September. We’ve gathered the season’s key developments and upcoming opportunities in thi…

title: Meet the 2026 ARIN Community Grant Recipients
description: We would like to congratulate the organizations receiving funding from the ARIN Community Grant Program this year! Senior Project Manager Amanda Gauldin shares details about their projects.

description: A transition to a new modern, modular, and containerized infrastructure for email services provided for ietf.org, iab.org, irtf.org, rfc-editor.org (including email lists) was completed on 11 September 2026.

description: The Independent Series Editor (ISE) selection criteria survey is live and we welcome your input on the capabilities and expectations the IAB should consider when selecting a future ISE. Please respond by 11 October 2026.

description: Post-quantum key establishment has moved from standards into deployment. Post-quantum authentication has not moved nearly as far, and specification work is no longer the only constraint. The IAB is holding a workshop in Prague on 11 and 12 October 2026 to bring deployment experie…

description: The IETF 126 Vienna meeting was held 18-24 July 2026 and the results of the post-meeting survey are now available.

description: Joe Clarke has been appointed as the new IETF Network Operations Center (NOC) Lead and in this post Joe introduces himself and sets out his priorities for the IETF Network.
